q.t: Find the area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 5 cm (in cm²).
q.e: A triangle is half of a parallelogram on the same base and height.

q.t: Find the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 4 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Slide the end triangle across and it becomes a 9 × 4 rectangle.

q.t: Which is the formula for the area of a trapezium with parallel sides a, b and height h?
q.e: Two copies, one turned round, make a parallelogram of base a + b.

q.t: Find the area of a rhombus with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm (in cm²).
q.e: ½ × d₁ × d₂: the rhombus fills half of the 20 × 15 rectangle around it.

q.t: A rectangle has area 28 in² and one side 4 in. The other side is (in in):
q.e: Area ÷ known side.

q.t: Two rectangles have the same perimeter. Their areas are:
o: Equal only if both are squares
q.e: A 1 × 9 and a 5 × 5 rectangle both have perimeter 20, but areas 9 and 25.

q.t: The height used in the area of a triangle must be:
q.e: Height is the straight-up distance from the base to the opposite vertex.

q.t: What is the area of an A4 sheet, 21 cm × 29.7 cm (in cm²)?
q.e: Length × width.

q.t: How many square metres make 1 hectare?
q.e: A hectare is a square 100 m by 100 m.

q.t: 1 ft² equals how many in²?
q.e: 1 ft = 12 in, so a square foot is 12 × 12 square inches.

q.t: Quadrilateral ABCD has diagonal AC = 22 cm and perpendiculars of 3 cm from B and D. Area (in cm²)?
q.e: Two triangles on base AC: ½ × 22 × 3 each.

q.t: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm and height 4 cm (in cm²).
1 in = 2.54 cm. How many cm² is 1 in²?
q.e: Square the conversion factor for areas: 2.54².

q.t: Convert 161.29 cm² to in².
q.e: Divide by 6.4516.

q.t: Triangles on the same base and between the same parallel lines have:
q.e: Same base and same height give the same ½ × b × h.

q.t: A rhombus has area 96 cm² and one diagonal 16 cm. Find the other diagonal (in cm).
A trapezium has area 105 cm², height 7 cm and one parallel side 12 cm. Find the other parallel side (in cm).
A 'house' shape is a rectangle 12 m by 8 m with a triangle of height 5 m on top of the 12 m side. Area (in m²)?
1 km² equals how many m²?
All parallelograms on the same base between the same parallels have equal areas. Their perimeters:
o: Grow as they get more slanted
q.e: Same height, but the slanted sides get longer.

q.t: A regular hexagon is cut into a trapezium, a rhombus and an equilateral triangle. Ratio of their areas?
q.e: The hexagon is 6 small equilateral triangles: trapezium 3, rhombus 2, triangle 1.

q.t: A rhombus has side 13 cm and one diagonal 10 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Half-diagonals 5 and 12 (5-12-13), so the diagonals are 10 and 24: ½ × 10 × 24.

q.t: Which trapezium has area 144 cm²?
o: Parallel sides 10 and 14 cm, height 12 cm
Parallel sides 10 and 14 cm, height 6 cm
Parallel sides 12 and 12 cm, height 6 cm
Parallel sides 6 and 18 cm, height 6 cm

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, BD = 26 cm and perpendiculars from A and C to BD are 12.8 cm and 11.2 cm. Area (in cm²)?
A trapezium has the same area as a square of side 12 cm. Its parallel sides are 10 and 14 cm. Height (in cm)?
M and N are midpoints of XY and XZ in triangle XYZ. Area of XMN is what fraction of XYZ?
q.e: Half the base and half the height: ½ × ½.

q.t: A path of width 2 m surrounds a 20 m × 10 m park. Area of the path (in m²)?
q.e: Outer 24 × 14 = 336 minus the park 200.

q.t: Doubling every length of a shape multiplies its area by:
q.e: Area scales by the square of the length factor: 2².

q.t: Convert 10 in² to cm².
A hexagon is a 10 cm × 6 cm rectangle with a triangle of height 4 cm on each 6 cm side. Area (in cm²)?
A trapezium has parallel sides 25 cm and 11 cm, and non-parallel sides 15 cm and 13 cm. Area (in cm²)?
q.e: Cutting off a parallelogram leaves a 14-15-13 triangle whose height is 12 (from area 84 on base 14).

q.t: The mid-line of a trapezium (joining midpoints of the slanted sides) is 15 cm and the height is 8 cm. Area (in cm²)?
q.e: The mid-line equals ½(a + b), so area = mid-line × height.

q.t: A quadrilateral has perpendicular diagonals 18 cm and 25 cm. Area (in cm²)?
q.e: ½ × d₁ × d₂ works for any quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals.

q.t: A rhombus has the same area as a triangle with base 24.8 cm and height 16.5 cm. One diagonal is 22 cm. Find the other (in cm).
q.e: Triangle area 204.6; ½ × 22 × d = 204.6.

q.t: A regular octagon of side 5 m is a rectangle 11 m × 5 m plus two trapeziums (parallel sides 5 and 11 m, height 4 m). Area (in m²)?
Equilateral triangle vs square, both of side s. Which is bigger?
o: The square (more than twice the triangle)
q.e: Triangle ≈ 0.433s², square = s².

q.t: ZYXW is a trapezium (ZY ∥ WX), A is the midpoint of XY, and ZA meets WX produced at B. Then area of ZYXW equals area of:
q.e: ∆ZAY ≅ ∆BAX, so swapping them keeps the area.

q.t: To change an isosceles triangle into a rectangle of equal area (Śulba-Sūtra), you:
o: Cut along the altitude and fit the two halves together
Cut off the top and throw it away
q.e: The two right-triangle halves make a rectangle of width b/2 and height h.

q.t: A rectangle 8 cm × 3 cm becomes a rhombus of equal area. Possible diagonals?
A trapezium's parallel sides are in the ratio 2 : 3, 12 cm apart, area 360 cm². Shorter parallel side (in cm)?
